findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is instantiated directly, bypassing the DI container/feature-flag wiring that swaps in `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when calendar-cache is disabled; the cache-status groupBy query will run and be surfaced in the UI even when the feature is off

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:23 — throws a plain `Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a tRPC `TRPCError` (e.g. NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN); non-TRPCError exceptions become a generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR so the client shows an unhelpful error toast for what is really a 403

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:30 — uses raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` instead of `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential`, bypassing the repository abstraction (and its invalidation side effects) and sidestepping the feature-flag mock

[Low/data] packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:174 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` doesn't filter on `expiresAt`, so expired cache entries are still reported as healthy "Cache Status / Last updated" to the user

[Low/api] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 — `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` assumes every entry has a non-null `credentialId`; a null credentialId would make the Prisma groupBy `{ in: [..., null] }` throw and break the whole connectedCalendars query

[Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88 — `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` hardcodes the en-US locale so the timestamp won't match the user's locale/format, unlike the surrounding i18n'd strings

[Low/test_gap] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts — no tests added for the new mutation (ownership check, delegation rejection, cache deletion), nor for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or `updateManyByCredentialId`; nothing exercises the new paths

[Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:66 — `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; on GNU/Linux sed this treats `''` as a filename and fails (or creates a stray file), breaking the env update on Linux dev machines

[Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:6 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script location; running the script from the repo root will target `<repo>/../.env` outside the project

[Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:31 — the delete-cache mutation's `onSettled` doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike the disconnect mutation), so the displayed cache timestamp can remain stale unless the parent happens to pass an `onSuccess` that refetches

[Low/performance] apps/web/package.json:11 — `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` will hit the npm registry and install `tsx` on the fly if not already present, making `dev:cron` network-dependent and non-reproducible; `tsx` should be a devDependency invoked via the package manager

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is instantiated directly, bypassing the DI container/feature-flag wiring that swaps in `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when calendar-cache is disabled; the cache-status groupBy query will run and be surfaced in the UI even when the feature is off

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` the diff explicitly imports and instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();`) instead of using an abstraction. The diff also shows an `ICalendarCacheRepository` interface and a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods log “due to calendar-cache being disabled”, suggesting there is (or is intended to be) some feature-flag/wiring to swap implementations. While the diff doesn’t show the DI container/flag wiring itself (so it’s not fully verifiable that this *will* break the disabled mode), the change is a concrete architectural coupling introduced by the diff and could prevent using the mock/disabled behavior in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:63 — `hasCache` is independent of `canDisconnect`, so a delegation-based Google connection (org-owned credential, userId null) will render "Delete cached data" but `deleteCacheHandler` requires `credential.userId === user.id` and will always reject, showing a destructive action guaranteed to fail

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` and is not gated by `canDisconnect` (which is false when `delegationCredentialId` is set). This means delegation-based Google credentials can still render the "Delete cached data" action and call `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.mutate({ credentialId })`. However, `deleteCacheHandler` only allows deletion when a `credential` exists with `id: credentialId` AND `userId: user.id` (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id, userId }})`). For any credential not owned by the current user (which delegation credentials commonly are), the mutation will deterministically throw "Credential not found or access denied", so the UI exposes a destructive action that is guaranteed to fail for that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022 — `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` only matches SelectedCalendars by `credentialId`; for delegated Google connections SelectedCalendars have `delegationCredentialId` set and `credentialId` null, so `updatedAt` is never bumped and "Last updated" silently doesn't work for delegation users

adjudication.rationale: The UI “Last updated” added in this diff is driven by `cacheUpdatedAt` (from `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` grouping on `calendarCache.updatedAt`) and passed into `CredentialActionsDropdown`. It is not derived from `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. While the diff does add `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, the finding’s claim that this breaks the displayed “Last updated” for delegation users relies on unstated schema/behavior (e.g., delegated SelectedCalendars having `credentialId = null` and needing `delegationCredentialId`) and doesn’t match how “Last updated” is actually computed in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:30 — uses raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` instead of `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential`, bypassing the repository abstraction (and its invalidation side effects) and sidestepping the feature-flag mock

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteCache.handler.ts` calling `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` directly, while a repository abstraction exists (`ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential()` with a mock implementation that no-ops when calendar-cache is disabled). This is a concrete, diff-grounded architecture/consistency issue: the new TRPC handler bypasses the repository layer (and therefore any feature-flag switching to the mock / centralized side effects). However, the diff does not prove any actual broken behavior or “invalidation side effects” that would make this a definite correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:174 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` doesn't filter on `expiresAt`, so expired cache entries are still reported as healthy "Cache Status / Last updated" to the user

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, the `groupBy` query only filters by `credentialId` and computes `_max.updatedAt`, but it does not filter out rows where `expiresAt` is in the past. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` uses this result to set `cacheUpdatedAt` and the UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) treats any non-null `cacheUpdatedAt` as `hasCache`, expired cache rows can still produce a non-null "Last updated" and show cache as present even if it should be considered expired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 — `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` assumes every entry has a non-null `credentialId`; a null credentialId would make the Prisma groupBy `{ in: [..., null] }` throw and break the whole connectedCalendars query

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, `credentialIds` is passed to `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, whose signature is `credentialIds: number[]` (added in this diff). That, plus multiple usages like `calendar.credentialId`/`connectedCalendar.credentialId` throughout the diff, implies `credentialId` is a non-null `number` in the `connectedCalendars` items. The diff provides no evidence that `credentialId` can be `null`, so the claimed `{ in: [..., null] }` Prisma failure is not verifiable from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts — no tests added for the new mutation (ownership check, delegation rejection, cache deletion), nor for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or `updateManyByCredentialId`; nothing exercises the new paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds several new, nontrivial code paths (a new authed TRPC mutation `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` with an ownership check and `calendarCache.deleteMany`, a new repository method `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy`, and `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId` plus a new call to it in `GoogleCalendarService`). The diff shows no accompanying test additions exercising these behaviors. However, the finding’s mention of “delegation rejection” is not reflected in `deleteCache.handler.ts` (it only checks `credential.userId`), so that part is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:6 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script location; running the script from the repo root will target `<repo>/../.env` outside the project

adjudication.rationale: The new script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` defines `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 6 in the diff) and never normalizes it relative to the script’s directory (e.g., via `DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)`). In bash, `../.env` is resolved relative to the current working directory. If run from the repo root as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, it will target `<repo>/../.env` outside the project, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:31 — the delete-cache mutation's `onSettled` doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike the disconnect mutation), so the displayed cache timestamp can remain stale unless the parent happens to pass an `onSuccess` that refetches

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only defines `onSuccess`/`onError` and does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or any other invalidation) the way `disconnectMutation` does in its `onSettled`. From the diff, the cache timestamp shown in the dropdown comes from `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (`connectedCalendars.handler.ts` enriches results with `cacheUpdatedAt`). Without invalidation, the UI will only refresh if the optional `onSuccess?.()` callback causes a refetch, which is an implicit/fragile contract rather than being handled within the mutation like the disconnect case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] apps/web/package.json:11 — `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` will hit the npm registry and install `tsx` on the fly if not already present, making `dev:cron` network-dependent and non-reproducible; `tsx` should be a devDependency invoked via the package manager

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `apps/web/package.json` script `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. Using `npx` can execute a package that is not locally installed, potentially downloading it at runtime, which makes the script network-dependent and less reproducible compared to invoking a declared devDependency via the package manager. The diff does not show whether `tsx` is already a dependency, but the concern is directly tied to the introduced `npx tsx` usage.
